note: Best published lower bounds for C(n) known to us on 2026-10-03. n64 and n100 were re-verified against their published point sets with evaluate.py and verify.py. n16 and n32 are quoted in the paper as C(16) = 28 and C(32) = 56 (from its reference [56]); no point set for them was checked here. No value is claimed optimal by us. Sizes without an entry (for example 48, 80, 128) have no published value that we found.

exceeded_by.found: 2026-10-03, by the seed solver solvers/noisosceles (symmetric + greedy_victim)
exceeded_by.checks: evaluate.py, verify.py, and a direct test of every ordered triple as in the notebook's verify_construction; unpublished, not yet reviewed by a person
exceeded_by.note: The published text presents 56 as optimal. The same solver never exceeds the published values at n = 7, 8, 9, 10, 16, 27, and an exhaustive search with this pack's definition gives 6, 7, 9 at n = 4, 5, 6, as published.
